description: Before March 2026 the member had paid nothing out of pocket, and none of the $150 in-network deductible was met. The EOB lists three dermatology claims, each an office visit (a copay) and a skin biopsy (20% coinsurance after the deductible). Claim 1's biopsy goes entirely to the deductible, and claim 2's biopsy finishes the deductible, with the member paying 20% of the rest; the cover shows the deductible fully met. Nevertheless claim 3's biopsy is charged its whole plan-approved amount as deductible again, instead of 20% coinsurance. The biopsy lines put more than $150 toward the deductible, which no correct EOB can show. The member owes only 20% coinsurance on claim 3's biopsy.

sources.what: A PPO with a deductible must have a single one; this plan's $150 in-network deductible applies once a year to coinsurance services, then 20% (note C1)
sources.source: eCFR, 42 CFR 422.101(d)(1), Requirements relating to basic benefits (single deductible for local PPO plans; other services may be waived from it), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.101; eCFR, 42 CFR 422.111(b)(2), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.111
